title: All the consorts of Ravana lament
introduction: All the consorts of Ravana lament, recollecting the valour of Ravana and with a stunning surprise of how he has been killed by an ordinary mortal. They feel sorry that, had Seetha been restored by Ravana to Rama, this major disaster would not have befallen them.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये युद्धकाण्डे दशाधिकशततमः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 110th chapter in Yuddha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
रावणम् निहतं दृष्ट्वा राघवेण महात्मना |
अन्तःपुराद्विनिष्पेतू राक्षस्यः शोककर्शिताः
verses.iast:
rāvaṇam nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghaveṇa mahātmanā |
antaḥpurādviniṣpetū rākṣasyaḥ śokakarśitāḥ
verses.translation: Seeing Ravana killed by the great-souled Rama, the female-demons were stricken with grief and rushed out from their gynaecium.

verses.devanagari:
वार्यमाणः सुबहुशो वेष्टन्त्यः क्षितिपांसुषु |
विमुक्तकेश्यः शोकार्ता गावो वत्सहता यथा
verses.iast:
vāryamāṇaḥ subahuśo veṣṭantyaḥ kṣitipāṃsuṣu |
vimuktakeśyaḥ śokārtā gāvo vatsahatā yathā
verses.translation: Even though impeded now and then by their maid servants, they were rolling in the dust of the streets, with their hair dishevelled, tormented as they were with grief like cows that had lost their calf.

glosses.meaning: in the dust on the floor

verses.devanagari:
उत्तरेण विनिष्क्रम्य द्वारेण सह राक्षसैः |
प्रविश्यायोधनं घोरं विचिन्वन्त्यो हतं पतिम्
आर्यपुत्रेति वादिन्यो हा नाथेति च सर्वशः |
परिपेतुः कबन्धाङ्कां महीं शोणितकर्दमाम्
verses.iast:
uttareṇa viniṣkramya dvāreṇa saha rākṣasaiḥ |
praviśyāyodhanaṃ ghoraṃ vicinvantyo hataṃ patim
āryaputreti vādinyo hā nātheti ca sarvaśaḥ |
paripetuḥ kabandhāṇ^kāṃ mahīṃ śoṇitakardamām
verses.translation: Issuing out of the northern gate along with demons and penetrating into the terrific battle-field, searching for their husband, who had been killed and crying out, "Ah my lord! Ah my husband!" they all ran hither and thither on the ground which was covered with headless trunks and rendered muddy with blood."

glosses.meaning: they all ran hither and thither
which was covered with headless trunks

verses.devanagari:
ता बाष्पपरिपूर्णाक्ष्यो भर्तृशोकपराजिताः |
करेण्व इव नर्दन्त्यो विनेदुर्हतयूथपाः
verses.iast:
tā bāṣpaparipūrṇākṣyo bhartṛśokaparājitāḥ |
kareṇva iva nardantyo vinedurhatayūthapāḥ
verses.translation: Those women, who were overcome with grief about the death of their husband, having their eyes filled with tears, loudly lamented like female-elephants who had lost the leader of their herd.

glosses.meaning: who were overcome with sorrow about the death of their husband
having their eyes filled with tears
who had lost the leader of their herd.

verses.devanagari:
ददृशुस्ता महाकायं महावीर्यं महद्युतिम् |
रावणं निहतं भूमौ नीलाञ्जनचयोपमम्
verses.iast:
dadṛśustā mahākāyaṃ mahāvīryaṃ mahadyutim |
rāvaṇaṃ nihataṃ bhūmau nīlāJṇjanacayopamam
verses.translation: Those women saw the gigantic Ravana, who was endowed with a great strength and invested with a great splendour, lying killed on the ground, like a heap of black collyrium.

glosses.meaning: who was endowed with a great strength
and invested with a great splendour
like a heap of black collyrium.

verses.devanagari:
ताः पतिं सहसा दृष्ट्वा शयानं रणपांसुषु |
निपेतुस्तस्य गात्रेषु छिन्ना वनलता इव
verses.iast:
tāḥ patiṃ sahasā dṛṣṭvā śayānaṃ raṇapāṃsuṣu |
nipetustasya gātreṣu chinnā vanalatā iva
verses.translation: Suddenly seeing their husband lying in dust of the battle-field, those women fell down on his limbs, like uprooted wild creepers.

verses.devanagari:
बहुमानात्परिष्वज्व काचिदेवं रुरोद ह |
चरणौ काचिदालम्ब्य काचित्कण्ठेऽवलम्ब्य च
verses.iast:
bahumānātpariṣvajva kācidevaṃ ruroda ha |
caraṇau kācidālambya kācitkaṇṭhe'valambya ca
verses.translation: A woman wept, embracing him out of great regard, another woman clinging to his feet and another, catching hold of his neck.

verses.devanagari:
उत्क्षिप्य च भुजौ काचिद् भूमौ सुपरिवर्तते |
हतस्य वदनं दृष्ट्वा काचिन्मोहमुपागमत्
verses.iast:
utkṣipya ca bhujau kācid bhūmau suparivartate |
hatasya vadanaṃ dṛṣṭvā kācinmohamupāgamat
verses.translation: A woman rolled over the ground, with her arms thrown up. On seeing the face of her deceased husband, another woman fell into a swoon.

glosses.meaning: the face of her deceased husband

verses.devanagari:
काचिदङ्के शिरः कृत्वा रुरोद मुखमीक्षती |
स्नापयन्ती मुखं बाष्पैस्तुषारैरिव पङ्कजम्
verses.iast:
kācidaṇ^ke śiraḥ kṛtvā ruroda mukhamīkṣatī |
snāpayantī mukhaṃ bāṣpaistuṣārairiva paṇ^kajam
verses.translation: Keeping Ravana's head in her lap, a woman, looking at his face, wept moistening that face with her tears, as dew drops moisten a lotus-flower.

verses.devanagari:
एवमार्ताः पतिं दृष्ट्वा रावणं निहतं भुवि |
चुक्रुशुर्बहुधा शोकाद्भूयस्ताः पर्यदेवयन्
येन वित्रासितः शक्रो येन वित्रासितो यमः |
येन वैश्रवणो राजा पुष्पकेण वियोजितः
गन्धर्वाणामृषीणां च सुराणां च महात्मनाम् |
भयं येन रणे दत्तं सोऽयं शेते रणे हतः
verses.iast:
evamārtāḥ patiṃ dṛṣṭvā rāvaṇaṃ nihataṃ bhuvi |
cukruśurbahudhā śokādbhūyastāḥ paryadevayan
yena vitrāsitaḥ śakro yena vitrāsito yamaḥ |
yena vaiśravaṇo rājā puṣpakeṇa viyojitaḥ
gandharvāṇāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca surāṇāṃ ca mahātmanām |
bhayaṃ yena raṇe dattaṃ so'yaṃ śete raṇe hataḥ
verses.translation: "That Ravana, by whom Indra was thrown into fear, Yama was struck with terror, by whom Kubera the king was deprived of Pushpaka the aerial car, and by whom fear was caused on the battle-field in the Gandharva the celestial musicians, in the sages and the great-souled gods, lies killed in the battle-field."

verses.devanagari:
असुरेभ्यः सुरेभ्यो वा पन्नगेभ्योऽपि वा तथा |
भयं यो न विजानाति तस्येदं मानुषाद् भयम्
verses.iast:
asurebhyaḥ surebhyo vā pannagebhyo'pi vā tathā |
bhayaṃ yo na vijānāti tasyedaṃ mānuṣād bhayam
verses.translation: "This danger has come from a mortal to him, who did not conceive any fear from the demons or the gods or even the serpents for that matter!"

glosses.meaning: who did not conceive any fear
even the serpents for that matter!.

verses.devanagari:
अवध्यो देवतानां यस्तथा दानवरक्षसाम् |
हतः सोऽयं रणे शेते मानुषेण पदातिना
verses.iast:
avadhyo devatānāṃ yastathā dānavarakṣasām |
hataḥ so'yaṃ raṇe śete mānuṣeṇa padātinā
verses.translation: "Here lies killed in battle, by a pedestrian man coming from Ayodhya, that Ravana, who was incapable of being killed by gods and even so by devils and demons too."

glosses.meaning: who was incapable of being killed

verses.devanagari:
यो न शक्यः सुरैर्हन्तुं न यक्षैर्नासुरैस्तथा |
सोऽयं कश्चिदिवासत्त्वो मृत्युं मर्येन लम्भितः
verses.iast:
yo na śakyaḥ surairhantuṃ na yakṣairnāsuraistathā |
so'yaṃ kaścidivāsattvo mṛtyuṃ maryena lambhitaḥ
verses.translation: "He who could not be killed by gods, Yakshas and demons alike, could be killed by a mortal like one devoid of strength."

verses.devanagari:
एवं वदन्त्यो रुरुदस्तस्य ता दुःखिताः स्त्रियः |
भूय एव च दुःखार्ता विलेपुश्च पुनः पुनः
verses.iast:
evaṃ vadantyo rurudastasya tā duḥkhitāḥ striyaḥ |
bhūya eva ca duḥkhārtā vilepuśca punaḥ punaḥ
verses.translation: Thus uttering, those women of Ravana, wailing as aforesaid, burst into tears. They once more and repeatedly lamented, stricken, as they were, with grief (as follows):

glosses.meaning: stricken as they were with grief.

verses.devanagari:
अशृण्वता तु सुहृदां सततं हितवादिनाम् |
मरणायाहृता सीता राक्षसाश्च निपातिताः
एताः सममिदानीं ते वयमात्मा च पातितः |
verses.iast:
aśṛṇvatā tu suhṛdāṃ satataṃ hitavādinām |
maraṇāyāhṛtā sītā rākṣasāśca nipātitāḥ
etāḥ samamidānīṃ te vayamātmā ca pātitaḥ |
verses.translation: "For your own death, Seetha was borne away by you, who did not listen to your near and dear ones, who always offered friendly counsel to you. The demons were struck down. Here, stand we (your consorts) as well as your own self, struck down now."

glosses.meaning: to your near and dear ones
as well as your own self

verses.devanagari:
ब्रुवाणोऽपि हितं वाक्यमिष्टो भ्राता विभीषणः
धृष्टं परुषितो मोहात्त्वयात्मवधकाङिक्ष्णा |
verses.iast:
bruvāṇo'pi hitaṃ vākyamiṣṭo bhrātā vibhīṣaṇaḥ
dhṛṣṭaṃ paruṣito mohāttvayātmavadhakāṇ^ikṣṇā |
verses.translation: "Though tendering salutary advice to you, Vibhishana your beloved brother, was harshly scolded through ignorance by you, who sought your own destruction."

verses.devanagari:
यदि निर्यातिता ते स्वात्सीता रामाय मैथिली
न नः स्याद्व्यसनं घोरमिदं मूलहरं महत् |
verses.iast:
yadi niryātitā te svātsītā rāmāya maithilī
na naḥ syādvyasanaṃ ghoramidaṃ mūlaharaṃ mahat |
verses.translation: "If you had restored Seetha a princess of Mithila to Rama, this appallingly terrific disaster, which has robbed us of every root, would not have befallen us."

glosses.meaning: which has robbed us of every root

verses.devanagari:
वृत्तकामो भवेद्भ्राता रामो मित्रकुलं भवेत्
वयं चाविधवाः सर्वाः सकामा न च शत्रवः |
verses.iast:
vṛttakāmo bhavedbhrātā rāmo mitrakulaṃ bhavet
vayaṃ cāvidhavāḥ sarvāḥ sakāmā na ca śatravaḥ |
verses.translation: "If you had restored Seetha to Rama, Vibhishana your brother would have had his desire fulfilled. Rama would have been in the company of our allies. All of us would have been spared the curse of widowhood and our enemies would not have realized their ambition."

glosses.meaning: in the company of our allies
all of us (would have been) avidhavaaH = spared the curse of widowhood
and our enemies na would not have

verses.devanagari:
त्वया पुनर्नृशंसेन सीतां संरुन्धता बलात्
राक्षसा वयमात्मा च त्रयं तुल्यं निपातितम् |
verses.iast:
tvayā punarnṛśaṃsena sītāṃ saṃrundhatā balāt
rākṣasā vayamātmā ca trayaṃ tulyaṃ nipātitam |
verses.translation: "By you, however, who forcefully captivated Seetha cruelly, the demons, we (your consorts) and your own self all the three have been destroyed all at once."

verses.devanagari:
न कामकारः कामं वा तव राक्षसपुंगव|
दैवं चेष्टयते सर्वं हतं दैवेन हन्यते
verses.iast:
na kāmakāraḥ kāmaṃ vā tava rākṣasapuṅgava |
daivaṃ ceṣṭayate sarvaṃ hataṃ daivena hanyate
verses.translation: "O the excellent demon! Your act of following your own free will, may not be the reason for your destruction, either for, all is being run by a divine power, struck and ruined by the divine power."

glosses.meaning: act of following your own free will
may not be the reason either

verses.devanagari:
वानराणाम् विनाशोऽयं राक्षसानां च ते रणे |
तव चैव महाबाहो दैवयोगादुपाग्तः
verses.iast:
vānarāṇām vināśo'yaṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca te raṇe |
tava caiva mahābāho daivayogādupāgtaḥ
verses.translation: "This destruction of the monkeys, your demons as also yourself, in the battle, has happened at the juncture of the Providence (alone), O the great armed!"

glosses.meaning: at the juncture of the providence (alone).

verses.devanagari:
नै वार्थेन न कामेन विक्रमेण न चाज्ञया |
शक्या दैवगतिर्लोके निवर्तयितुमुद्यता
verses.iast:
nai vārthena na kāmena vikrameṇa na cājJṇayā |
śakyā daivagatirloke nivartayitumudyatā
verses.translation: "The course of destiny, when ready to bear fruit, cannot be diverted either by money, or by wish, or by valour or even by command in this world."

verses.devanagari:
विलेपुरेवं दीनास्ता राक्षसाधिपयोषितः |
कुरर्य इव दुःखार्ता बाष्पपर्याकुलेक्षणाः
verses.iast:
vilepurevaṃ dīnāstā rākṣasādhipayoṣitaḥ |
kurarya iva duḥkhārtā bāṣpaparyākulekṣaṇāḥ
verses.translation: Those consorts of Ravana, depressed as they were and afflicted with grief, with their eyes full of tears, thus lamented like female ospreys.

glosses.meaning: with their eyes full of tears
